start.text:
Sergeant Gorman is standing where he has evidently been standing for some hours.

'You'd be Blackthorn's. Smith said he'd send someone and I said I'd not stop him.' He looks at you a moment longer than the sentence needed. 'Moretti. That is a name I wrote down on the twenty-seventh.'

choices.text: Did anyone hear anything the night before?
I'd like the key to the cash box.

morning.text:
'Half seven. Door fast, shutters up, and the landlord on the stair saying nobody had seen him since Sunday. We took the frame off rather than the bolt, because I wanted the bolt kept as it was.'

He says the last part slowly, as a man who has been overruled before and would like it in the record this time.

night.text:
'Two neighbours heard the bell go eleven and both say his light was already out. Surgeon says midnight.' He lets that stand a second. 'I'm police. I write what the surgeon writes. I don't have to like the arithmetic.'

'There were three that week, and I was told they were three.'

keys_ask.text:
'The box stays sealed until the estate's settled. That's the form of it.'

He says it the way a man says a thing he would rather be argued out of.

choices.text: Offer him something for his trouble.
Suggest, gently, that he wants to hand it over.

keys_paid.text:
The coins go into his glove without either of you looking at them.

'Back before dark. And Moretti — if you find the thing the surgeon missed, you bring it to me before you bring it to the Church.'

keys_pressed.text:
He hands it over before he has finished deciding to, and then stands there holding the shape of an objection he can no longer find.

You put the key in your pocket. He will remember this conversation wrongly for a week, and after that he will remember it correctly, and you will not be able to do anything about that.

start.text:
Mr. Franky has his hat in both hands and has not put it down since you arrived.

'I let them in. The police. I have the keys to eleven doors on this side of the borough and I have never once had to use one for that.' He turns the hat around. 'You were at his readings. I saw you on the stair in May.'

choices.text: Tell me about the last week.
What did he bring into this house?

week.text:
'He stopped going out. He nailed the shutters himself — I heard him at it on the Thursday, and when I knocked he talked to me through the door about the weather.'

'He asked me whether the walls between the rooms were solid. Not the doors. The walls.'

pledge.text:
'A book. Black boards, no title, and he carried it about like a man carrying a full cup.' He looks at the ceiling. 'He told me it was older than the Kingdom, which I said was a thing men say, and he did not laugh.'

'It isn't in there now. I have been up and down those rooms with the sergeant and it isn't in there now.'

cass.text:
'The one who delivered it.' Something crosses his face and he folds it away. 'He came back after. Twice. Said he had a bill outstanding, and I told him the police had it sealed, and he thanked me and went, and he had not asked which rooms.'

'A man collecting a bill asks which rooms.'

bye.text: 'Find me something I can tell the other tenants.'

start.text:
Hanass is calm in the way that takes practice, and has been for eight days.

'A shame. He was a pleasant gentleman and he paid in full.' He does not ask what you want. 'I carry things from one address to another. What is in them is the business of the address.'

choices.text: The last ferry over the Tussock is at seven.
Whose hand cut the page out of his transcription?
Read what he is not saying.

alibi.text:
'Over the water by nine. My lodgings are on the far bank and I keep regular hours, and I passed the lamplighter on the bridge road and a woman with two dogs, and you may ask them both.'

He offers the dogs before anybody has asked for anything.

broken.text:
You put the ferryman's hours to him, plainly, and watch him arrive at the end of the sentence a little after you do.

He starts three answers. The third one is 'I may be wrong about the day,' and he hears himself say it.

ledger.text:
'I do not read what I carry.'

He says it too quickly, and then again more slowly, which is worse. 'One leaf. Out of a copy. Not out of the book — the book was to be returned entire, that was the whole of the arrangement—'

And there he stops, because he has just told you there was an arrangement.

read.text:
You ask the one thing he has spent eight days preparing not to be asked, and it lands somewhere behind his eyes.

What comes back is not the answer. It is the cellar: cold at his back, coal in his hands, and above him, through the boards, a voice reading steadily in a language it had no business being fluent in — and then not stopping when it should have stopped.

bye.text: He wishes you a good evening, and means it, which is the unpleasant part.

start.text:
Sil Mowbray is coiling a wet rope badly and in no hurry.

'Ferry's done. Ferry's done at seven, same as it's been done at seven since my father had the licence.'

choices.text: Who's been buying odd things off the market?

ferry.text:
The coins vanish into the rope coil.

'Seven, and that's the summer table. No bridge nearer than four mile up. A man on the far bank at nine got there before seven or he got there wet.'

vane.text:
'There's a gentleman does his buying through other gentlemen. Alzuhod. Never seen him, never met a man who has, and I have been asked three times this month whether I ferried a black book across.'

'Wanting a thing back is one price. Wanting it back quiet is another, and he is paying the second.'

halloway.text:
'The young gentleman with the shutters?' He spits over the side, unhurried. 'Come down here twice in a fortnight asking after the deep water. Not for a boat. For the depth.'

'A man wants to know how deep a thing goes, he is thinking about putting something in it. He never did, mind. I'd have seen.'

bye.text: He goes back to ruining the rope.
